title: New York Taiwan Center 紐約台灣會館
content_html:
New York Taiwan Center (紐約台灣會館) is a non-profit 501(c)(3) organization established in 1987 in Flushing, Queens, by donations from Taiwanese Americans in the Greater New York area. It is recognized as the first community center established by Taiwanese immigrants in the United States and is one of the largest Taiwanese American non-profit organizations in the country. The center serves as a hub connecting the Taiwanese diaspora with both the broader New York community and Taiwan, and is home to the Greater New York Taiwanese American Organizations Alliance, which links nearly thirty Taiwanese American organizations across New York and New Jersey.

The center’s programs are organized around three areas. Its Senior Center serves approximately 500 members and offers fitness activities, arts and leisure courses, health seminars, and social services; members have also formed a chorus, a Taiwanese opera troupe, and dance groups that perform in the community. Cultural and arts programming includes lectures, concerts, and performances by visiting groups from Taiwan, with a particular focus on Taiwanese American Heritage Week each May. Community and educational programs include children’s rhythmic gymnastics and dance, adult education in ink painting, dance, and yoga, youth hip-hop classes, and an extensive Taiwanese book collection. The center also partners with external organizations including the Korean Community Services of Metropolitan New York, the North America Taiwanese Medical Association, and New York Awakening for legal services for new immigrants.
